talk.definition: To speak with someone in order to share thoughts, news, or ideas.
talk.exampleUsage: We sat in the living room to talk about our family plans.

speak.definition: To use your voice to say words or communicate in a language.
speak.exampleUsage: Please speak clearly so everyone in the room can hear you.

say.definition: To express a thought, greeting, or statement in spoken words.
say.exampleUsage: Remember to say thank you when someone helps you.

tell.definition: To communicate information, a story, or instructions to someone.
tell.exampleUsage: Grandfather loves to tell stories from his childhood.

ask.definition: To put a question to someone or request help or permission.
ask.exampleUsage: Raise your hand if you would like to ask a question.

answer.definition: To reply in words or writing to a question, call, or message.
answer.exampleUsage: Take your time to read each question before you answer.

explain.definition: To make an idea or problem clear by describing it in detail.
explain.exampleUsage: The teacher used a diagram to explain how the water cycle works.

describe.definition: To say what someone or something is like by giving details.
describe.exampleUsage: Can you describe the bag you lost at the train station?

announce.definition: To make a plan, decision, or piece of news known publicly.
announce.exampleUsage: The principal will announce the winners of the reading contest today.

declare.definition: To state something firmly, openly, or officially.
declare.exampleUsage: The judges met to declare the official results of the competition.

whisper.definition: To speak very softly, typically with breath rather than a fully voiced sound.
whisper.exampleUsage: Please whisper in the library so you do not disturb people reading.

shout.definition: To call out or speak in a very loud voice so others can hear from far away.
shout.exampleUsage: The coach had to shout across the field to gather the players.

yell.definition: To cry out loudly, often when warning someone or calling from a distance.
yell.exampleUsage: Did I hear someone yell my name from across the courtyard?

scream.definition: To make a loud, high-pitched cry because of sudden fear or pain.
scream.exampleUsage: The sudden flash of lightning made the toddler scream in surprise.

murmur.definition: To say something in a low, quiet, and indistinct voice.
murmur.exampleUsage: We heard the visitors murmur quietly as they admired the calligraphy.

mumble.definition: To speak quietly and unclearly with your mouth partly closed.
mumble.exampleUsage: Do not mumble your words when giving a presentation.

stutter.definition: To speak with involuntary pauses or repetitions of initial sounds.
stutter.exampleUsage: Speaking slowly and calmly helped him not to stutter.

stammer.definition: To speak with disruptions such as repetitions, prolongations, or pauses; often synonymous with stutter.
stammer.exampleUsage: Nervous speakers sometimes stammer during their first sentence.

sing.definition: To produce musical tones and melodies using your voice.
sing.exampleUsage: We heard the birds sing in the garden trees at sunrise.

chant.definition: To repeat words or phrases rhythmically, often together in a group.
chant.exampleUsage: The crowd began to chant encouragement for their local team.

discuss.definition: To talk about a subject with others in order to exchange ideas or reach a decision.
discuss.exampleUsage: Let us meet tomorrow morning to discuss the project schedule.

debate.definition: To argue different sides of a topic in a structured, formal way.
debate.exampleUsage: University students gathered to debate the best ways to save energy.

argue.definition: To give reasons for or against something, or to disagree heatedly in words.
argue.exampleUsage: It is better to listen patiently than to argue over small details.

agree.definition: To have the same opinion as someone else or say yes to a plan.
agree.exampleUsage: All members of the committee agree that safety comes first.

disagree.definition: To hold a different opinion from someone else.
disagree.exampleUsage: We can respectfully disagree and still work well together.

negotiate.definition: To discuss terms with others in an effort to reach an agreement.
negotiate.exampleUsage: The buyer and seller met to negotiate the price of the house.

persuade.definition: To influence someone to do or believe something, often by giving reasons.
persuade.exampleUsage: He tried to persuade his brother to join the morning walk.

convince.definition: To make someone certain that a statement or idea is true.
convince.exampleUsage: The clear test results helped convince the team to update the design.

suggest.definition: To put forward an idea or plan for other people to consider.
suggest.exampleUsage: Which book would you suggest for a beginner learning Arabic?

propose.definition: To formally put forward a plan or idea for consideration at a meeting.
propose.exampleUsage: The engineer stood up to propose a safer design for the bridge.

write.definition: To form letters or words on paper or a screen to record a message.
write.exampleUsage: Please write down the address so you do not forget it.

read.definition: To look at written or printed words and understand their meaning.
read.exampleUsage: I like to read a chapter of a book every evening.

type.definition: To write text by pressing keys on a keyboard or phone screen.
type.exampleUsage: Please type your response into the form and press submit.

email.definition: To send an electronic message or document over the internet.
email.exampleUsage: I will email you the meeting notes before the end of the day.

text.definition: To send a short written message to someone using a mobile phone.
text.exampleUsage: Please text your parents as soon as your flight lands safely.

print.definition: To produce text or images on paper using a printer.
print.exampleUsage: Please print two copies of the boarding pass before we leave.

publish.definition: To prepare and issue a book, article, or report for the public to read.
publish.exampleUsage: The university press plans to publish the new dictionary next spring.

edit.definition: To check and improve written text by correcting errors and making it clearer.
edit.exampleUsage: Always edit your essay for spelling and grammar before handing it in.

draft.definition: To write the first version of a letter, speech, or report.
draft.exampleUsage: He spent the morning working to draft the project proposal.

revise.definition: To review and update a piece of writing to improve its clarity and accuracy.
revise.exampleUsage: The author decided to revise the final chapter based on reader feedback.

gesture.definition: To move your hands or head to express an idea or direction.
gesture.exampleUsage: The host smiled and made a polite gesture toward the dining room.

nod.definition: To move your head down and up to show agreement, understanding, or greeting.
nod.exampleUsage: He gave a polite nod to show that he understood the instructions.

shake-head.definition: To move the head from side to side to show disagreement or refusal.
shake-head.exampleUsage: She shook her head to show that the answer was no.

point.definition: To direct someone's attention toward something by extending your finger.
point.exampleUsage: The guide used a map to point toward the historic mosque.

wave.definition: To move your hand from side to side in the air to greet someone or say goodbye.
wave.exampleUsage: The children stood at the window to wave goodbye to their cousins.

shrug.definition: To raise and lower your shoulders briefly to show that you do not know something.
shrug.exampleUsage: When asked why the train was late, the passenger could only shrug.

signal.definition: To use a hand movement, light, or sound to give an instruction or warning.
signal.exampleUsage: Always signal before turning your car into another lane.

mime.definition: To act out an action or object using only hand and body movements without words.
mime.exampleUsage: Since the room was noisy, he had to mime drinking water from a cup.

sign.definition: To communicate using a sign language in this lesson’s gesture context.
sign.exampleUsage: An interpreter stood beside the speaker to sign for deaf guests.

wink.definition: To close and open one eye quickly as a friendly signal.
wink.exampleUsage: The grandfather gave a friendly wink as he handed the child a gift.
